Rules.lead: Want to understand what's happening during a game? Start here. Learn who's who, how points are scored and when a jam ends.
Rules.rolesSub: Each team normally has up to 5 skaters on the track: 1 jammer + 4 blockers. One of those blockers can be the pivot.
Rules.jammerDesc: The only player who scores points. You can spot the jammer by the star on the helmet cover.
Rules.jammerNote: Goal: get through the pack, then pass opponents.
Rules.blockerDesc: Helps their own jammer forward and tries to slow the other jammer down with positioning and blocks.
Rules.blockerNote: A team has at most four blockers; the pivot is one of them.
Rules.pivotDesc: A special blocker with a stripe on the helmet cover. Under certain conditions the jammer can pass the star to the pivot.
Rules.rulesHeading: What you need to know to watch
Rules.rule1Title: A jam lasts up to 2 minutes.
Rules.rule1Body: The jam can end sooner if the lead jammer calls it off.
Rules.rule2Body: The jammer earns points by lapping opponents.
Rules.rule3Body: They try to help their own jammer and hold back the other one.
Rules.rule4Title: A penalty can send a player to the penalty box.
Rules.rule4Body: There the player misses part of the jam.
Rules.tipBody: Follow only the jammers at first. Look for the two stars on the helmets. Watch who gets through the pack first and which opponents they pass after that.
Rules.tipNote: As a beginner you don't need to watch all the blockers, officials and tactics at once. If you can follow the jammers, you already understand a big part of the game.
Rules.passTitle: A pass = the jammer legally gets past an opponent
Rules.passBody: As a new spectator you can think of it like this: the jammer wears the Star, skates in the right direction and gets past an opponent without the pass being cancelled by a foul or by being out of bounds.
Rules.passStep1Body: Look for the star on the helmet cover.
Rules.passStep2Body: The jammer goes from behind the opponent to in front of them.
Rules.passStep3Body: The officials officially decide whether the pass and its point count.
Rules.passTip: Rule of thumb: see the jammer legally get past a blocker? That's a moment the jammer can score. The official score is set by the officials.
Rules.leadHeading: How can a jam end early?
Rules.leadTitle: The lead jammer can call off the jam ✋
Rules.leadBody1: The lead jammer is the first eligible jammer to earn lead status by getting through the pack according to the rules.
Rules.leadBody2: The lead jammer can stop the jam before the 2 minutes are up by repeatedly putting both hands on their hips.
Rules.leadBody3: No lead jammer? Then no jammer can end the jam early this way. The jam runs to its full length, unless the game is stopped for another reason.
Rules.wallBody: Several blockers work together to hold back an opponent or make room for their own jammer.
Rules.packBody: The pack is the group of blockers at the heart of the game. That's where much of the tactical work happens.
Rules.isolateBody: Getting a blocker away from the rest of the group means that player can't help as well.
Rules.jamSub: Use these five steps as a viewing guide during a real game.
Rules.step1Body: The jammers start behind the Jammer Line. The blockers line up in front and form the pack.
Rules.step2Body: Both jammers try to get through the blockers. Blockers help their own jammer and hinder the other.
Rules.step3Body: The first eligible jammer to earn lead status becomes lead jammer.
Rules.step4Body: The jammer keeps going and can earn points by lapping opponents.
Rules.step5Body: The lead jammer can call off the jam with hands on hips. Otherwise the jam runs until time is up.
Rules.example: Example: Jammer A gets lead. A comes through the pack again and goes for points. Jammer B is closing in. A puts both hands on their hips → the jam stops. Points earned under the rules stay on the board.
Rules.glossarySub: Click a term for a short explanation.
Rules.term1Body: A period of play of up to two minutes.
Rules.term2Body: The largest group of blockers from both teams that are close enough together to count as one group.
Rules.term3Body: The first eligible jammer to earn lead status. Only the lead jammer can call off the jam early.
Rules.term4Body: The jammer's helmet cover with the star.
Rules.term5Body: The pivot is the blocker with the stripe on the helmet cover.
Rules.term6Body: When a jammer passes an opponent for the second time relative to that opponent, it can earn an extra point.
Rules.term7Body: The sin bin. A player who gets a penalty sits out here for a set time.
Rules.term8Body: Inside the boundaries of the track.
Rules.term9Body: Outside the area where blockers are allowed to take part in blocking under the rules.
Rules.term10Body: Non-Skating Official: an official who isn't on skates and keeps track of things like score, penalties or time.
Rules.video1Body: Open the video on YouTube and use the explanation above to spot the jammers and the pack.
Rules.video2Body: Watch the second video, then try to spot the five steps of a jam yourself.
Rules.q1: How many jammers does each team normally have on the track?
Rules.q2: What is the maximum number of blockers per team?
Rules.q4: Who can call off the jam early?
Rules.q5: How do you recognise the pivot?
Rules.q5a2: By a stripe on the helmet cover
Rules.quizPerfect: Perfect, you can follow the basics!
Rules.quizGood: Nice work, you've got the key terms down.
Rules.quizRetry: Read the explanation again and have another go.
Rules.sourceBody: This explanation is deliberately simplified for new spectators. For official definitions, exceptions and the full rules, the current WFTDA rulebook applies.

Venue.title: Venue & info
Venue.houseIntro: So everyone has a good day, we keep to a few agreements inside the hall.
Venue.houseDefault1: Respect skaters, officials and the audience.
Venue.houseDefault2: No food or drinks in the hall except water in a closable bottle.
Venue.houseDefault3: Keep bags out of the track-side area, use the locker rooms.
Venue.houseDefault5: First aid or questions? Head to the organizer's table by the entrance.
Venue.foodBody: Snacks and sandwiches are for sale in the cafeteria, vegan options too. Bring your own water bottle.
Venue.firstAidBody: The first aid post is marked with a green cross near the entrance. In an emergency head to the organizer's table.
Venue.changingBody: One dressing room per two teams, with a shower.
Venue.parkingBody: Free parking around the venue. From Nijmegen Central Station take bus 6 towards Weezenhof, stop Horstacker.
Venue.floorBody: Sports floor with skate coating. Advised wheel hardness: 92a to 95a.
Venue.sponsorsBody: This tournament is supported by our sponsors. Logos follow closer to the event date.

Toernooi.title: About the tournament
Toernooi.lead: Everything you need to know about the Small Teams Tournament by Roadkill Rollers Nijmegen on 21 November 2026.
Toernooi.introHeading: What is the Small Teams Tournament?
Toernooi.introBody: The Small Teams Tournament is a roller derby tournament for small teams: a fun day full of short, fast matches, for skaters and spectators alike. New to roller derby? On the rules page we explain what to look for in just a few minutes.
Toernooi.formatBody: This tournament features 8 teams of 8 skaters, split across 2 pools. Each team plays every other team in its pool, so three pool games per team. There are 13 games in total, including one final. After the pool phase, the best teams from each pool advance to the final. Games are spread across the day as evenly as possible, with rest between each game.
Toernooi.gamesBody: Each game lasts 20 minutes with no clock stop. Each team gets one team time-out per game. There is no official review. Four penalties in a game means a foul out. In the pool phase teams play in black and white; in the final they play in their own colours.
Toernooi.scheduleBody:
Preliminary schedule:
11.00: officials meeting
12.00: tournament start
18.00: tournament end

The two pools alternate, so you have at least 20 minutes between your games. There is also one half-hour break.
